images.text:
Sally: George, tell me more about what you and your friends did outside when you were a kid.
George: We had such a fun time after school and on the weekends. Typically, we would throw on some old clothes, ride our bikes down to the river and spend hours splashing around. It was such a splendid way to spend sunny afternoons.

Sometimes we would splurge on new comics, splay them out on the ground and recite the stories of each one. We loved acting out the different characters. I remember once, Teddy splattered some cola on my favorite comic. We made him take the bottle and drink up the whole thing  there and then. I almost split my pants from laughter! I used to get splinters in my feet and hands from running around in the woods barefoot.

My mom caught on to what we were doing and told me off a few times. I think she secretly loved that we were so carefree and wild. I think we all turned out happy and healthy and I think that our childhood really contributed to that.

In English pronunciation, it is common to pronounce consonant blends. These are a combination of two or more consonant sounds.
The consonant blend /spl/ has three sounds: s + p + l.
Try saying these three sounds together. Concentrate carefully on the position of your tongue, teeth and lips for each sound. Try to move smoothly between each sound so that they become one sound.
It's a good idea to look in the mirror and watch your mouth as you make the sound.
When you say a long sentence in English, you break it into distinct parts, each with its own intonation. You use the rise and fall of your voice to show the listener when you are or are not finished.
You break long sentences into parts, called clauses. Each clause has its own subject and verb (and sometimes object).
Typically,// we would throw on some old clothes,// ride our bikes down to the river// and spend hours splashing around.//
At the end of each clause, you use rising intonation to show the listener that the sentence is not finished.
